questions.q: A's salary is 40% more than B's. If B's salary increases by 20% and A's increases by x%, then A's new salary becomes 25% more than B's new salary. What is the value of x?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: B ka base 100 maan. 100 -> 120. A naya hoga 120 ka 1.25 times, jo 150 hota hai. A tha 140, ho gaya 150. Jump 10 ka hai 140 par. Option 7.14% turant dikhna chahiye kyuki $\frac{1}{14}$ fraction standard hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai aise karna hai... B = 100, A = 140. Naya B = 120. Naya A = $120 \times 1.25 = 150$. A badha 10 se (140 to 150). $x = \frac{10}{140} \times 100$. Zero se zero kaat, $\frac{1}{14}$ bacha. Answer 7.14%.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Multiplier method. A = 1.4 B. Naya B = 1.2 B. Naya A = 1.25 * (1.2 B) = 1.5 B. Pehle A 1.4 B tha, ab 1.5 B hai. Growth = $\frac{0.1}{1.4} = \frac{1}{14}$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Ratio trick se fraction $\frac{1}{14}$ direct yaad hona chahiye, CGL me yahi time bachega!

questions.q: The income of a person first increases by 25% and then decreases by 25%. What percentage is the new income of the original income?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: Successive Change (The Chain Reaction)

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Same percentage badh kar ghat raha hai, matlab loss hi hoga. Aur loss nikal ke 100 se minus karna hai kyuki 'new income' pucha hai, 'change' nahi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Same percentage increase/decrease me humesha $-\frac{x^2}{100}$ ka net change aata hai. Yaha $\frac{25^2}{100} = 6.25$ ka decrease. Original 100 tha, toh bacha $100 - 6.25 = 93.75$%. Seedha tick maar!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
ConceptFormula
A. Same +x% and -x%1. $-\frac{x^2}{100}$% (Always Loss)
B. Diff +a% and +b%2. $a + b + \frac{ab}{100}$%

Future Exam Takeaway: CDS me ye standard trap hai, question dhyan se padh ki 'change' pucha hai ya 'new value'.

questions.q: The price of an article decreased by 8% every year. If the difference between the price at the end of the third and fourth year is 69, then 40% of the price at the end of the second year is?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: Successive Change (The Chain Reaction)

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: 3rd aur 4th year ke beech ka difference purely 3rd year ki value ka 8% hi toh hoga! Piche calculate karna hai (reverse successive). Digital sum ya multiples check kar sakte ho, par calculation aasan hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai aise karna hai... $8\% \text{ of } P_3 = 69 \implies P_3 = \frac{6900}{8}$. Ab $P_3$ aaya kaise? $P_2$ me 8% ghata ke, yaani $P_2 \times 0.92 = P_3$. Toh $P_2 = \frac{6900}{8 \times 0.92}$. Humein $40\%$ (yaani 0.4) of $P_2$ chahiye: $0.4 \times \frac{6900}{8 \times 0.92} = 375$. Calculation ko end tak hold kar!

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Let starting price be P. $P_3 = P \times (0.92)^3$. Difference $P_3 - P_4 = P_3 - P_3(0.92) = P_3(0.08) = 69$. Step by step nikalne me time waste hota hai, seedha reverse shift lagao.

Best Exam Approach: Method 1, combined with intermediate step skipping.

questions.q: A man's annual income has increased by 5000 but the tax on income that he has to pay has reduced from 15% to 12%. While in both the situations, 30% of the income tax is tax-free. Find the initial income, if equal tax is paid in both cases?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: CPR (Constant Product Ratio)

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Tax = Income $\times$ Tax Rate. Jab Tax (Product) constant hai, toh Income aur Tax Rate inversely proportional honge. Rate 15 se 12 hua (Ratio 5:4). Toh Income 4 se 5 hui hogi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Tax free portion (30%) dono taraf cut jayega, ignore kar. Tax rate ratio = 15:12 = 5:4. CPR lagao: Tax same hai toh Income ratio = 4:5. Gap 1 unit ka hai. 1 unit = 5000 (increase). Toh initial income 4 units = 20000. Pen nahi uthana tha isme!

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Equation: $70\% \text{ of } 15\% \text{ of } x = 70\% \text{ of } 12\% \text{ of } (x + 5000)$. $15x = 12x + 60000 \implies 3x = 60000 \implies x = 20000$.

Future Exam Takeaway: CPR method CGL Mains me aag laga dega! Product constant dekhte hi cross-ratio lagao.

questions.q: Rahul had to appear for a test in four subjects. In the first three subjects the maximum marks were 50 each, in which Rahul secured 60% on an average. In the fourth subject Rahul scored 54 marks and his overall percentage is 64%. What were the maximum marks in the fourth subject?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling / Basic Arithmetic

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: 3 subjects ka total 150. Usme 60% laya (yaani 90 marks). 4th me 54 marks. Total marks 144 jo ki 64% hai total max ka. Sidha equation dikh rahi hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Total scored = 90 (first 3) + 54 (4th) = 144. Ye 144 overall 64% hai. So, $64\% = 144 \implies 100\% = \frac{144}{64} \times 100 = 225$ (Digital sum check: $9/1 = 9$, 225 ka digital sum bhi 9, match). Total max marks 225. Pehle 3 subjects ka max 150 tha. Toh 4th ka hoga $225 - 150 = 75$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Let 4th subject max marks be x. $\frac{90 + 54}{150 + x} = \frac{64}{100}$. Solve for x. Wahi 75 aayega.

Future Exam Takeaway: C9 (Digital Sum) verification step me fraction divide karte time bahut useful hai, confidence deta hai!

questions.q: The population of a town is 3,11,250. The ratio of women to men is 43:40. If there are 24% literate among men and 8% literate among women, the total number of literate persons in the town is?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: JSM (Junior Satisfaction Method) / Weighted Average

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Pura lamba chauda number 3,11,250 dekh ke darna mat. Ratio dekho: Total 83 parts = 311250. 83 ek prime hai, toh pakka perfectly katega. Base value nikal aur apply kar.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai aise karna hai... W = 43x, M = 40x. Total 83x = 311250 $\implies$ x = 3750 (unit digit se hint le, $3 \times 5 = 15$). Literate Men = $24\%$ of $40x = 9.6x$. Literate Women = $8\%$ of $43x = 3.44x$. Total literate = $13.04x$. Total = $13.04 \times 3750 = 48900$. Digital Sum check: 13.04 (DS=8) * 3750 (DS=6) = 48 -> DS=3. Options me check kar, 48900 ka DS = 4+8+9=21 -> 3. Match!

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Standard tarika yahi hai bas bacche pehle population ko exact men/women me todte hain, phir percentage nikalte hain. Wo 'Maha-Paap' hai.

Future Exam Takeaway: Variables (x) me hi percentage calculate kar aur end me multiply kar. CDS me time bachana hi asli game hai!

questions.q: A and B contested in an election in a village. A got x% of the total number of votes and B got (x – 20)% of the total number of votes and the ratio of the total number of votes obtained by A to B is 3:2. Find the total number of voters in the village, if (x/2)% of the total number of votes is 1200.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: Cross-Product Method / Unitary Scaling

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Ratio 3:2 dekhte hi dimag me aana chahiye ki inka gap 1 unit ka hai. Percent me gap x aur (x-20) ka 20% hai. 1 unit = 20%!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai, question me hi answer chhipa hai. Gap ratio me 1 unit hai, aur percent me 20. Toh A ka vote 3 unit = 60%, B ka vote 2 unit = 40%. Direct mil gaya x = 60. Ab diya hai $(x/2)\%$ of Total = 1200. Matlab $30\%$ of Total = 1200. Toh $10\% = 400$, and $100\% = 4000$. Pen chhoone ki saza-e-maut hai is question me!

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Equation banayega: $\frac{x}{x-20} = \frac{3}{2}$. Cross multiply: $2x = 3x - 60 \implies x = 60$. Fir wahi same steps.

Future Exam Takeaway: Ratio scaling is king. Jab relative gap percentage me diya ho, direct ratio parts se equate kar de.

questions.q: A man spends 80% of his income. His income has increased by 25%, but his expenditure remains the same. By what percent have his savings increased?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling / Basic Arithmetic

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Kharcha badha hi nahi! Yaani income me jo bhi extra paisa aaya, wo pura ka pura bachat (savings) me chala gaya. Direct logic.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai, Income = 100, Exp = 80, Sav = 20. Income ho gayi 125. Exp abhi bhi 80 hai. Toh new Savings = 45. Kitni badhi? 25. Original savings 20 thi. Percentage jump = $\frac{25}{20} \times 100 = 125\%$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): JSM se bhi soch sakta hai, par isme values itni choti aur simple hain ki basic direct equating is visually much faster.

Best Exam Approach: Sirf extra paise ka flow track kar. Extra 25 aaya aur wo direct 20 ki bachat par gaya. $25/20$ ka growth seedha 125% hai.

questions.q: In an exam, 44% of students passed in only History and 36% of students passed in only Economics. If 6% of the students failed in both subjects and the number of students who failed in Economics is 125, then find the number of students who failed in History.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: 5. Unitary Scaling

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Venn diagram banane ka time waste bilkul nahi karna. 'Failed in Economics' ka direct matlab hota hai wo students jo sirf History me pass hue hain plus jo dono me nipat gaye (failed in both). Data dekhte hi percentages dimag me add hone chahiye.



Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Failed in Economics = (Passed in Only History) + (Failed in Both). Yaani $44\% + 6\% = 50\%$. Question cheekh-cheekh ke keh raha hai ki ye $50\%$ ki value 125 bacche hai. Toh multiplier kya hua? $125 / 50 = 2.5$ times. Ab hume nikalna hai 'Failed in History', jo hoga (Passed in Only Economics) + (Failed in Both) = $36\% + 6\% = 42\%$. Toh actual value nikalne ke liye Unitary Scaling lagao: $42 \times 2.5 = 105$. Khel khatam, 10-15 seconds me ans mark kar aur aage badh!

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Let Total students = $100x$. Only History (H) = $44x$, Only Economics (E) = $36x$, Failed Both = $6x$. Passed in Both = $100x - (44x + 36x + 6x) = 14x$. 'Failed in Economics' ka matalab wo jo E circle ke bahar hain = Only H + Failed Both = $44x + 6x = 50x$. Given $50x = 125 \implies x = 2.5$. We need 'Failed in History' = Only E + Failed Both = $36x + 6x = 42x$. Therefore, actual count = $42 \times 2.5 = 105$.

Future Exam Takeaway: SSC CGL aur CDS me jab bhi 'Failed in Subject A' pooche, toh ek golden rule raat le: Failed in A = Only Pass in B + Fail in Both. Yeh single property Venn diagram ke questions ko bina circle draw kiye verbally uda deti hai.

questions.q: A heavy industrial machine was purchased for 2,00,000. Its value depreciated by b% in the first year and then appreciated by a% in the second year due to an upgrade. Both a and b are natural numbers. If the value of the machine after the second year was more than its original purchase price, and a - b = 8 find the lowest possible depreciated value of the machine at the end of the first year.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: Successive Change (The Chain Reaction) / Number Theory

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Ye sawal purely CAT level trap hai jo SSC Mains me aa sakta hai. Net change positive hona chahiye, yaani $a - b - \frac{ab}{100} > 0$. $a - b = 8$ diya hai. So, $8 - \frac{ab}{100} > 0 \implies ab < 800$. Humein first year ke baad ki value lowest chahiye, yaani depreciation 'b' maximum hona chahiye.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai aise karna hai... $ab < 800$ and $a = b + 8$. Put kar: $b(b+8) < 800$. Ab options se hint le ya hit & trial kar. Agar $b=20$ rakha toh $20 \times 28 = 560$ (aur bada ho sakta hai). Agar $b=25$ rakha toh $25 \times 33 = 825$ (800 cross kar gaya, fail). Agar $b=24$ rakha toh $24 \times 32 = 768 < 800$. Perfect! Max possible natural number $b = 24$. Toh 1st year depreciation 24% hai. Value = $200000 \times (1 - 0.24) = 152000$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Mathematically quadratic inequality solve karni padegi: $b^2 + 8b - 800 < 0$. Roots are around 24.something. Since b is a natural number, largest integer $b = 24$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Absolute hardest trap! Hamesha Net successive change formula me inequalities laga kar extreme case pakdo.

questions.q: There are 70 students in a class, but only 6/7 of them play at least one indoor game (Chess, Carrom, and Scrabble). It is given that 28.56% of the total students play Chess, 42.85% play Scrabble, and 57.14% play Carrom. Exactly 6 students play both Chess and Scrabble but not Carrom, 14.28% play both Scrabble and Carrom but not Chess, and 5 students play all 3 games. Find the number of students who play Chess and Carrom but not Scrabble.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Dekh bhai, saari percentages khatarnak dikh rahi hain par sab $\\frac{1}{7}$ ki family se hain! $14.28\\% = \\frac{1}{7}$, $28.56\\% = \\frac{2}{7}$, etc. Seedha total 70 par in fractions ko lagao aur exact integer values nikalo. Active bacche sirf $\\frac{6}{7} \\times 70 = 60$ hain.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Total active students (Union) = 60.
Ab direct values nikal out of total 70:
Chess (C) = $\\frac{2}{7} \\times 70 = 20$
Scrabble (S) = $\\frac{3}{7} \\times 70 = 30$
Carrom (M) = $\\frac{4}{7} \\times 70 = 40$
'Only C & S' = 6
'Only S & M' = $\\frac{1}{7} \\times 70 = 10$
'All 3' = 5
Hamein nikalna hai 'Only C & M', isko $x$ maan le.

Venn diagram ka sabse standard formula laga:
$$Union = n(C) + n(S) + n(M) - n(C \\cap S) - n(S \\cap M) - n(C \\cap M) + n(All)$$
Yahan overlaps mein 'Only 2' + 'All 3' aata hai.
$$60 = 20 + 30 + 40 - (6+5) - (10+5) - (x+5) + 5$$
$$60 = 90 - 11 - 15 - x - 5 + 5$$
$$60 = 64 - x \\implies x = 4$$
Seedha 4 aagaya! Option 2 is correct.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Venn diagram bana aur inner to outer region fill kar. Let 'Only C' = $c$, 'Only S' = $s$, 'Only M' = $m$.
Scrabble circle total is 30:
$$s + 6 + 10 + 5 = 30 \\implies s = 9$$
Chess circle total is 20:
$$c + 6 + 5 + x = 20 \\implies c + x = 9$$
Carrom circle total is 40:
$$m + 10 + 5 + x = 40 \\implies m + x = 25$$
Total Union = $c + s + m + 6 + 10 + x + 5 = 60$
Substitute $s = 9$:
$$c + m + x = 30$$
Hamein pata hai $c = 9 - x$ aur $m = 25 - x$. Isme put kar de:
$$(9 - x) + (25 - x) + x = 30$$
$$34 - x = 30 \\implies x = 4$$

Future Exam Takeaway:
SSC CGL Mains me aisi percentages hamesha fractional family se hoti hain. Pehchaan aur fraction me tod, phir standard set theory formula chipka de! Time bacha, rank la!

questions.q: A cuboid tank has dimensions: length = 25 cm, breadth = 20 cm, and height = 16 cm. If the length is increased by 10%, the breadth is decreased by 20%, and the height is increased by 10%, what is the percentage change in volume?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: Successive Change (The Chain Reaction)

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Base dimensions (25, 20, 16) diye hain sirf darane aur time waste karne ke liye! Percentage change pucha hai, original values se koi matlab nahi. Net successive lagao.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai aise karna hai... $+10\%, -20\%, +10\%$. Pehle 10 aur -20 ka net nikalo: $10 - 20 - \frac{200}{100} = -12\%$. Ab is -12% ka bache hue +10% ke sath lagao: $-12 + 10 - \frac{120}{100} = -2 - 1.2 = -3.2\%$. Negative sign ka matlab decrease. 10 second me answer! is se better +10, +10 ka successive 21-20 +\frac{-20×21} {100} net 3.2 niklega successive seq jaruri noi 🫡😘

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Ratio method se dekho: $L: 10 \to 11$. $B: 5 \to 4$. $H: 10 \to 11$. Multiply kar: $500 \to 484$. Change = -16. $\% = \frac{-16}{500} \times 100 = -3.2\%$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Original data ignore karna aana chahiye jab answer relative (percentage) me pucha ho.

questions.q: A student appeared in 6 papers. The maximum marks are the same for each paper. His marks in these papers are in the proportion 5 : 6 : 7 : 8 : 9 : 10. Overall he scored 60%. In how many papers he received less than 60% marks?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling / Deviation

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Data proportion me diya hai aur final relative constraint (60%) par focus hai. Total marks obtained ratio ke terms me jodo, waha se maximum marks ki imaginary value nikal lo.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Sum of scores = $5+6+7+8+9+10 = 45x$. Ye 45x overall max marks ka 60% hai. Yaani $60\% = 45x \implies 100\% (Total Max) = \frac{45x}{60} \times 100 = 75x$. 6 papers ka Total Max 75x hai, aur sab equal hain. Toh 1 paper ka Max = $\frac{75x}{6} = 12.5x$. Kisi subject me 60% se kam aane ka constraint check karna hai. 12.5x ka 60% hota hai 7.5x. Toh kin subjects me 7.5x se kam hai? Pehle teen (5, 6, 7). Answer 3.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Algebraically assume Total Max = 600. Then 60% = 360. $45x = 360 \implies x=8$. Marks are 40, 48, 56, 64, 72, 80. Each paper max = 100. 60% of 100 = 60. Marks < 60 are 40, 48, 56 (3 papers). Same logic!

Best Exam Approach: Method 1 me ek ratio base calculation hai jo dimag me jaldi process hota hai.

questions.q: The population of country A decreased by p% and the population of country B decreased by q% from the year 2020 to 2021. Here 'p' is greater than 'q'. Let 'x' be the ratio of the population of country A to the population of country B in the given year. What is the percentage decrease in 'x' from 2020 to 2021?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: Successive Change / Variable Ratio Algebra

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Formula based hai. Ratio $x = \frac{A}{B}$. New ratio banega $x' = \frac{A(1 - \frac{p}{100})}{B(1 - \frac{q}{100})}$. Yaani old ke sath ek multiplier chipka hai $\frac{100-p}{100-q}$. Bas yahi se decrease fraction nikal lena hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai aise karna hai... New $x' = x \times \frac{100-p}{100-q}$. Decrease kitna hua? $(1 - \frac{100-p}{100-q}) \times x = \frac{(100-q) - (100-p)}{100-q} \times x = \frac{p-q}{100-q} \times x$. Percentage me badalne ke liye 100 se multiply karo base (x) ke respect me: $\frac{p-q}{100-q} \times 100$. Option A tick maar bina darr ke!

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Value assume karlo. Let A=100, B=100. Let p=20, q=10. Original x=1. New A=80, New B=90. New x = $\frac{80}{90} = \frac{8}{9}$. Decrease = $1 - \frac{8}{9} = \frac{1}{9}$. Percentage decrease = $\frac{100}{9}\%$. Options me p=20, q=10 dalo. A) $\frac{100(10)}{90} = \frac{100}{9}$. Match! Baki options match nahi karenge.

Future Exam Takeaway: Variables dekh ke blank mat ho, assumption method (Method 2) hamesha zinda rakhega.

questions.q: The price of a product is decreased by x% and then increased by x%. The final price becomes 10% less than the original. What is the value of x (approximately)?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: Successive Change (The Chain Reaction)

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Same x% up and down means strict loss of $\frac{x^2}{100}$%. Ye loss value 10% ke barabar hai. Seedha equation banega $x^2 = 1000$. Squares yaad hain toh answer aankh band karke aa jayega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai aise karna hai... $\frac{x^2}{100} = 10 \implies x^2 = 1000$. Square roots approximate karne ki trick lagao: $30^2 = 900$ aur $31^2 = 961$. Yani value 31 se thodi upar hogi. Option 31.6 is the only logical choice.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): $31.6^2 = 31.6 \times 31.6 \approx 998.56$, jo ki 1000 ke bohot karib hai. Exact $1000^{0.5} = 31.62...$

Future Exam Takeaway: Range estimation approach CGL Pre me 5-10 second me answers lock karne me madad karti hai.

questions.q: A person has to pay 20% tax on the first Rs. 9,000 earned, for the amount earned between Rs. 9,000 and Rs. 15,000 the tax is 25%, and for the amount earned more than Rs. 15,000 the tax is 30%. If he paid 23.33% of his income as tax, then what is his income?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: 3. JSM (Junior Satisfaction Method) / Unitary Scaling

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Overall average tax 23.33\\% (yaani $\\frac{7}{30}$) hai. Pehle 9,000 par 20\\%, agle 6,000 par 25\\%, aur 15,000 se upar bachi hui income $x$ par 30\\% tax lag raha hai. Total income $(15000 + x)$ ho jayegi.

Method 1 (PDF Solution - Remaining Income 'x' Method): Dekh bhai, Tutor ne board par PDF me exact aise hi lagaya hai:
Pehle 9,000 par tax = 20\\% of 9000 = 1800
Agle 6,000 par tax = 25\\% of 6000 = 1500
15,000 se upar bachi income = $x$, ispar tax = 30\\% of $x$

Total Tax = $1800 + 1500 + 30\\% \\text{ of } x$
Ye total tax poori income $(15000 + x)$ ka 23.33\\% (yaani $\\frac{7}{30}$) hai.

Equation set kar:
$$ 1800 + 1500 + \\frac{30}{100}x = \\frac{7}{30}(15000 + x) $$
$$ 3300 + \\frac{3x}{10} = \\frac{7}{30} \\times 15000 + \\frac{7x}{30} $$
$$ 3300 + \\frac{3x}{10} = 3500 + \\frac{7x}{30} $$
$$ \\frac{3x}{10} - \\frac{7x}{30} = 3500 - 3300 $$
$$ \\frac{9x - 7x}{30} = 200 $$
$$ \\frac{2x}{30} = 200 $$
$$ x = 3000 $$

Bacha hua amount $x = 3000$ aaya.
Toh Total Income = $15000 + x = 15000 + 3000 = 18000$.

Method 2 (PDF Solution - Double Alligation / JSM):
Step 1: First 9k @ 20\\%, Next 6k @ 25\\%. Ratio = 3 : 2.
Weighted average tax = $20\\% + \\frac{2 \\times 5\\%}{5} = 22\\%$.

Step 2: Ab Alligation lagao (Rs. 15000 @ 22\\% and Rs. $x$ @ 30\\% to get 23.33\\% = $\\frac{70}{3}\\%$):
Alligation ratio of values:
$$ (30 - \\frac{70}{3}) : (\\frac{70}{3} - 22) $$
$$ \\frac{20}{3} : \\frac{4}{3} = 5 : 1 $$
Agar 5 units = 15,000 hai, toh 1 unit ($x$) = 3,000.
Total Income = $15000 + 3000 = 18000$.

Method 3 (Test App Approach - Options Verification / Ninja Hack): Option A (18,000) check karo.
Slabs: $9000 + 6000 + 3000$
Tax = $1800 + 1500 + 900 = 4200$
$$\\frac{4200}{18000} = \\frac{7}{30} = 23.33\\%$$
Direct match in 10 seconds!

Best Exam Takeaway: Tutor ka $x$ wala linear equation basic setup ke liye mast hai, lekin exam me Options Substitution se solve karoge toh bina kisi calculation mistake ke 15 sec me question phod doge!

questions.q: The income of Amala is 20% more than that of Bimala and 20% less than that of Kamala. If Kamala's income goes down by 4% and Bimala's goes up by 10%, then the percentage by which Kamala's income would exceed Bimala's is nearest to
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling / Ratio Equalization

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Amala (A) common link hai. A aur B ka relation diya hai, fir A aur C (Kamala) ka. A ko barabar karne ke liye LCM lekar starting base fix kar, aage ki percentages smooth ho jayengi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai aise karna hai... A:B = 120:100 = 6:5. A:C = 80:100 = 4:5. A ko common kar (6 aur 4 ka LCM 12 hai). Ratio A:B:C = 12:10:15. Zero laga kar 120, 100, 150 kar le calculation aasan hogi. Ab C ko 4% down kar toh $150 - 6 = 144$. B ko 10% up kar toh $100 + 10 = 110$. Kamala Bimala ko kitne se exceed kar rhi hai? $144 - 110 = 34$. Percentage = $\frac{34}{110} \times 100 = \frac{340}{11} \approx 30.9\%$. Nearest 31%.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Direct fractions se ratio set karna, same logic. Agar variables loge (Let C = x) toh time waste hoga.

Future Exam Takeaway: 3 party relative percentage me hamesha 'Common Link' ka LCM le kar standard 100/1000 ki series banalo.

questions.q: Deepak spends 75% of his income, whereas Karan spends 80% of his income. Both of them save Rs. 7,500 each. The income of Sanjay is one-third of the sum of the income of Deepak and Karan. If Sanjay spends (7/9)th of his income, then find his savings.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: 5. Unitary Scaling

Dekh bhai aise karna hai, dono methods se pura bhaukaal tight rakhte hain.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique - Actual Base calculation):
Deepak spends 75%, so saves 25% (\\frac{1}{4}). Base Income = $7500 \\times 4 = 30000$.
Karan spends 80%, so saves 20% (\\frac{1}{5}). Base Income = $7500 \\times 5 = 37500$.
Sum of Incomes = $30000 + 37500 = 67500$.
Sanjay's Income = $\\frac{67500}{3} = 22500$.
Sanjay spends $\\frac{7}{9}$, so saves $\\frac{2}{9}$.
Savings = $\\frac{2}{9} \\times 22500 = 5000$.

Method 2 (Teri 'Zeher' Ratio Approach):
Savings barabar hain, seedha ratios equate kar!
$D \\times 25\\% = K \\times 20\\% \\Rightarrow \\frac{D}{K} = \\frac{4}{5}$. Total = 9 units.
Sanjay's savings in units = $9 \\times \\frac{1}{3} \\times \\frac{2}{9} = \\frac{2}{3}$ units.
Ab real value se link kar: Deepak's saving = $4 \\times \\frac{1}{4} = 1$ unit.
Question ke hisaab se, $1 \\text{ unit} = 7500$.
Sanjay's saving = $7500 \\times \\frac{2}{3} = 5000$. Dono hi method 15 second wale hain, zero algebraic variables ka masterstroke!
